text.p: SmartServer for KNX/EIB is a product which allows to remote clients (to visualization programs) to read and write data from KNX/EIB bus. SmartServer is designed for continuous running, it is present in the operating system as a service. SmartServer KNX/EIB keeps data in the cache, so their current values are available for clients continually. Server can be remotely administrated by web interface (HTTP/HTML).
Server provides for clients two interfaces: XMLSocket and line-oriented text TCP/IP interface.

li.p: operating system MS Windows XP SP2 and higher, XP Embedded SP2 and higher or Vista RTM and higher,
an active network connection for connection with clients and KNX/EIB,
on the KNX/EIB devices EIBNet/IP (it is part of a KNX standard).

text.p: The SmartServer installation packet (in the form of MSI file, MSI = Microsoft Installer) is installed after start-up automatically to Program Files\NeNo\EibSrv folder. During the installation, it is necessary to enter proper licence data (from licence certificate), or it is possible to install the SmartServer as a demo version.

il.caption: Compared to the full version, the demo version is limited as follows:

li.p: it allows to clients to perform only about 10000 clients operations collectively,
it provides data to clients only about 30 minutes after start-up,
the limitation does not stop the service and does not terminate connection with clients; the clients will stay connected, the server does not provide any data to them.

text.p: Installed SmartServer must be activated till 35 days after the installation. The activation can be performed remotely (with connection to Internet) or from the command line, but always with help of the tool (liccli), which is installed together with the SmartServer. If the SmartServer is not activated during the above shown 35 days, it will run as the demo version after lapse of this time.

The activation runs in two steps. In the first step there is obtained there is obtained a registration number, which is then sent to the technical support (of the seller). The technical support will record this number and will create an activation number based on it, which will send back. In the second step of activationthe activation number is applied.
The registration number is obtained with help of liccli tool as follows (record of operations in command line):

text.p: Caution: After the activation the SmartServer service (EIB/KNXServer) must be restarted. In computers with embedded operation system (Windows XP Embedded), it is further necessary to record changes of computer set-up on the disc and to restart the computer.

The SmartServer runs as a service of operation system and it starts immediately after installation. It loads all its settings (KNX/EIB objects, communication, EIBNet/IPinterface) from a text file on the disc (description, see bellow), which is allotted to the server with help of administrative web interface. The configuration file cannot be modified with help of the administrative interface, the file must be recorded on the disc by another way (locally, with help of RDP, VNC, etc.).

Without modification by the administrative interface, the server searches and loads, as starting file, default.cfg configuration file, which is located in the same folder, as the server program (EibSrv.exe). This starting configuration file is installed and contains also a list of all available settings also with brief comments.

Program running as the service has limited possibilities of interaction with user, therefore it is not possible to find out its proper loading from configuration file directly. Error messages about configuration are available in administrative interface only. The configuration can be checked also before its setting with help of tool of checkcfg.exe command line, which is delivered as a part of server installation.

Configuration files for server are text ones, structured to sections ones (section names are between [ a ] characters) and line oriented ones (parameters are recorded inside sections on independent lines).
Sample configuration files are stored in Examples folder with the server program.

text.p: [objects] and [blocks] sections summarize all definitions of KNX data items, which should be known to server and with which the server should communicate. For each data item, it is necessary to know its address(-es), data type and kind of its communication in the configuration. [objects] and [blocks] sections differ from each other by the kind of record of these data.

Both sections record definitions of objects to lines, [objects] requests complete information about data items on each line, on the contrary[blocks] defines one data type and one kind of communication for the whole group of data items, thus [objects] is well suitable for quick definition of several data items, whereas [blocks] allows larger structuring of the configuration.

In both sections, the data objects can be defined with help of objects, object, logged_objects, logged_object, logged_on_change_objects and logged_on_change_object parameters. Their distinguishing is simple: objects, logged_objects and logged_on_change_objects allow common definition of more data objects (each with one group address); object, logged_object and logged_on_change_object define one data object eventually connected with more group addresses (the model is the same as at connection of communication objects with group addresses at current EIB programming in ETS).

logged_on_change_object, logged_objects and logged_object parameters serve for definition of data objects, which changes in time will be recorded in administrative part of web interface (in Data history part). E.g. example configuration file 12 test-logged.cfg contains an example of use of monitored data objects.
In definition of data items, keywords according to the table are used.

Note: scaling255 extending type changes the standard function of EIS6 type. While the data item of scaling type offers the standard range 0100 (%) to clients, scaling255 data item communicates with clients with non-converted value in the range 0255.
The server in configuration uses keywords (the most frequent selections are shown in bolds) for determination of the way of communication according to the table .

f.table.label: tblBehavior
f.table.caption: Ways of communication of data objects

tr.td: Data item is not written to EIB, it contains the last value flown through the data bus.

As tracker, but at start of server, or at restoration of connection with KNX/EIB, it reads out by forced way the current value from EIB. An equipment must exist in EIB, which will respond this requirement.
Data item is written to EIB, it contains the last value written by some of clients, it does not accept values from EIB.
Data item is written to EIB and accepts values from EIB. It contains the last value either from EIB or from clients.
As transmitter_with_status, but at starting or at restoration of connection it reads out the value from EIB by forced way as well as tracker_init.

To avoid repeated entering of the type and kind of communication in definitions of objects, they are included to type and behaviour parameters. The second example defines the same objects, as the first two lines in example of use [objects].

There can be written a short description enclosed in quotes before each data object (group address). The description will appear in data log (in Data history web interface page). Example of description written to data object:

text.p: Next examples of record of data items can be found in files: 04 init-read.cfg (data items with forced initial loading), 06 complex-object.cfg (data items connected with more group addresses), 08 blocks.cfg (definition of data items with help of [blocks] section).

[read_start] contains parameters for control of initial loading, i.e. of the first loading of tracker_init and transmitter_with_status_init objects after start of the server (see the chapter ). The server loads such selected data objects in block procedurally and tries to load them all. To prevent an overloading of the data bus at starting (e.g., to allow recording to KNX just from the starting), the server puts delays between loadings of single data objects (delay parameter). If some of objects cannot be loaded, the server tries, after lapse of recovery delay ([interface] read_on_start_delay, the chapter ), to obtain them repeatedly by new loading. The server proceeds by this way, till it will not exhaust the permitted number of initial loadings (parameter [interface] read_on_start_repeat_count, see the chapter ).
If no problems occur in communication at starting, there is recommended to leave the initial values of parameters (e.g., not to enter read_start section to the configuration file).

dd.p: The highest number of loadings performed by the server for obtaining of concrete data object. The server will finish the loading of data object as soon as the equipment in KNX responds.
The starting value of this parameter is 1.
A delay between loadings of single data objects. If data are loaded successfully without any problems, then single requirements for loading to KNX data bus will be sent just with this delay. Example:
The starting value of this parameter is 150 (milliseconds).
A time, for which the server waits for the response. If nobody in KNX network responds till lapse of this time, the server repeats the request according to setting of repeat_count parameter.
The starting value of this parameter is 1500 (milliseconds).

text.p: The initial loading may (especially at large number of initialised data object) last relatively a long time. E.g., at loading of 100 data objects the obtaining of the value itself (without repetition and recovery) lasts in total 15 seconds (150ms100). Of course, during this time it is possible to load to the data bus arbitrarily, nevertheless, the data for clients need not be valid yet (in such case the server will return zero, false or empty text to clients).

text.p: [log] section determines the kind of listing of debugging and informative reports of the server. There may be many detail reports, therefore it is recommended to list only the error statuses during current operation.

[datalog] section is an additive one and determines the place, where the server will record the copies of reports of Data history of web interface. The rerouting of copies of listings can be used for storage of longer data history, because data in web interface are limited by number. In initial setting, the storage of data history, except of web interface, is not switched-on.

[httplog] section determines the place, where the server will record web access messages. Default settings of the [httplog] section is to use settings of [log] section. Recorded messages are in Common Log Format, which is the format broadly shared by all web servers. [httplog] log will contain access messages only, error messages (processing errors, etc.) are recorded according to [log] section settings.
The last [networklog] section offers separated logging of SDAP and XMLSocket client connecting and disconnecting. Default settings of the [networklog] section is to use settings of [log] section.

[web] section defines parameters necessary for proper run of web interface of the server. The SmartServer installation locates the data of web interface to the proper place, the contents of the configuration section [web] corresponds to this place.
It is recommended to leave the settings of this section without modifications.

Files in this root are available on the address http://[server]/SmartServer ([server] is replaced by the name or address of the computer, on which the server runs). The files stored straight in the root are the system ones (administrative interface uses them) and must not be modified. User’s data (need not be used) are stored to User folder in the root, then these data are available on the address http://[server]/SmartServer/User/…

text.p: [http_access_list] section defines a list of rules, which denies or allows access to server's web interface. Each rule (allowing or denying) is one IP address including network prefix length. During each client access, the server comes through all rules which correspond to client IP address and evaluates access permission found. The client is allowed to access if resulting permission is allow. Default permission is allow.
Rule format is:
text.p.type: allow | deny = <ipaddress>[/<prefix length>]

section.title: Import of data items from ETS

text.p: The definition of data items of the server may be significantly accelerated in cooperation with ETS program. ETS can (according to its configuration) export group addresses of the project to the text file determined for OPC server (KNX Association product, as well as ETS). This file (with ESF extension) can accept the server configuration and use all data items from it. ESF file need not contain always all necessary information, nevertheless, the server can deal with missing data (according to the setting, see below).
The server will accept the data objects from ESF file inside [objects] section with help of esf_adapt, esf_strict and esf_ignore parameters with the meaning according to table .

tr.td: Data items without accurate data type will be accepted, their type will be modified according to typical use and the configuration will be loaded.
Data items without accurate data type will be refused and the configuration will not be loaded (errors will be reported).
Data items without accurate data type will be ignored and the configuration will be loaded (the server will not know the data ones, without types of items).

text.p: All types recorded as EIS1EIS15 are considered for accurate data types. Inaccurate data types are shown in ESF file in the form, e.g. Uncertain (3 byte), which allows (as mentioned above), at use of esf_adapt parameter, to select a suitable type automatically. If this is not successful, then the loading of configuration will finish with error message.
At loading of esf_adapt configuration, the server will convert inaccurate types to accurate ones according to table .

f.table.caption: Replacement of inaccurately determined types in ESF file

At its run, the server can record information about current status and running operations. It can be useful, e.g., at solution of problems with communications. On the start, the listings are not switched-on, [log], [datalog], [httplog] and [networklog] configuration file sections serves for their switching-on and setting. Debugging information are not necessary for current operation.

The output of debugging information is the text and the line one, and this it is easily legible. The input setting of the server allows to monitor the listings with help of web interface, after modification of the configurationall data can be stored to the file. Messages of [log] and [networklog] sections have common formát (see below), [httplog] section uses Common Log Format, [datalog] section has special format.
The example of [log] section records:

The date and time of the listing are in the first part, in square brackets. All debugging listings are in UTC time, which is one hour less in comparison with the civil Czech time in winter, and two hours less in summer. Example: A listing with the time 18:06:03.828 was acquired on April 1st, so the corresponding civil time of acquirement is 20:06:03,828.

dl.caption: The second part, an independent letter, codes the kind of the report. The possibilities are as follows (they are classified from the most detail to the most important ones):

dd.p: debugging report, the second level of details
common report, additional information
debugging report, the first level of details
common report, warning against possible troubles at certain situation
debugging report, important information
common report, error of the protocol, status or program, the server is able to continue in operation
debugging report, information about the error
common report, fatal error of the program, the server is not able to continue in operation

dl.caption: The third part of the report distinguishes the origin of the report; reports from following sources appears in the server:

dd.p: Connection with KNX interface, information about EibNet/IP protocol.
Web server, information about page transfers to clients.
Net server for client connections, information about establishing and termination of connection and about transmission blocks.
SDAP server, information about commands and responses received through SDAP.
XMLSocket server, information about commands and responses received through XMLSocket.

text.p: Behind the third part in the debugging report there follows a text, which is not longer formalised and which contains any data (such ones, which the origin wants to show).

The most frequent reason for use of debugging reports is the communication with help of EibNet/IP protocol, i.e. the communication with KNX interface. The interface is an independent element outside the server control, which may be switched on or off independently, or which may be used by somebody else for connection with KNX. In every such case, the server has not connection with KNX and it is necessary to switch on the debugging listings for diagnostics of troubles.
The chapter is addressed to diagnostics and debugging listings as well.

The SmartServer supports both kinds of communication with KNX, which are usable for transmission of data. Other kinds, which serve for KNX configuration and programming, are not supported by the SmartServer. The SmartServer is not a tool for programming of elements in KNX data bus.

dl.caption: The kind of communication is governed by mode parameter of [device] section of the configuration file (see ). Following guide-post can be used for selection of the kind of communication:
dl.dt: Does the interface support tunnelling only?

dd.p: This is valid practically for all interfaces available on the market. tunnelling or tunnelling-NAT must be used.
Its name will probably contain router, or it will be some sort of PLC. Any kind of communication can be usedtunnelling, tunnelling-NAT or routing.
Nevertheless, because the router is determined just for transmission of data communication from KNX to IP network and back, it is recommended to select the kind of routing.

dl.dt: Does the server or interface occur behind the router?

dd.p: The only variant will be tunnelling-NAT probably.

dl.dt: Is the interface produced by other manufacturer than Siemens?

dd.p: There may be problems with tunnelling-NAT connection. Transfer through NAT is Siemens design, which evades KNX standard by this solution. On the other hand, the communication with the interface behaves according to customs in IP networks. In present time, also ETS supports the transfer through NAT, so it can be expected that also another producers than Siemens will support this kind of communication.

Nevertheless, till the tunnelling-NAT will be declared for standard solution, before its use it is necessary to verify (including connection behind NAT), if selected KNX interface does not have problems with it.

text.p: Routers in IP communications are located always between networks and logically connect them. Properly set router transmits all KNX operation between networks without problems, nevertheless, EIBNet/IP character may cause troubles in real cases.

dl.caption: Problem issues for EIBNet/IP may be:

dd.p: Communication by the way of routing runs with help of IP multicasting, when one sent packet can be received by more IP recipients. Used IP multicasting is easily recognizable according to IP addressmulticast addresses start with number 224 and higher (e.g. 225.100.1.5).Switches and routers must be able to recognize and properly send the IP multicasting, which is not always true. At selection of the switch and router for kind of communication of routing it is always necessary to assure knowledge of IP multicasting element.

NAT is a technology allowing exchanging of addresses and ports of senders and recipients in communication. The most frequent use of NAT is currently highly single-purpose onein home and office routersfor connection of smaller network to Internet. To allow transfer between the SmartServer and interface through such EIBNet/IP communication router, it is always necessary to adjust setting of the router (of course, the router must be able to do it).

EIBNet/IP communication is UDP, a permanent connection is not established between elements, therefore the router must know, which data should be forwarded and where. For successful transfer through NAT router there must be assured that the external packet (from Internet, from WAN interface of the router) will direct the router inside to real equipment (to computer with the SmartServer or KNX interface). Routers usually decide about routing according to the protocol type (UDP) and the port number (if port is not changed, then number 3671 is valid for EIBNet/IP). In their configuration then there will exist a rule (port forwarding, for triggering, server inside, etc.), which will perform the UDP communication on selected port of the equipment with internal IP address. An accurate configuration differs router from router, nevertheless, the router configuration can be managed by any network specialist.
The transfer of data packages with help of NAT from inside of the network out (to Internet) usually need not be configured by any way.

To allow the operation of EIBNet/IP communication between the SmartServer a the KNX interface, all NAT routers on the route must be set properly. Typical case is, e.g., an interconnection of two smaller networks through Internet, when both networks have NAT routers on their interfaces. Both these routers must have configured transfer of external EIBNet/IP packages to internal network.

dl.dt: Computer with more network cards, routers

dd.p: The tunnel communication in EIBNet/IP requires the client to announce to the server (KNX interface) its IP address (SmartServer) inside the data packet. The server will consequently send the response to this IP address. If a computer has more network cards (two Ethernet interface, Ethernet+WiFi, etc.), or if data pass through the router to another networks, then the communication by the way of tunnelling need not be successful.

In the first case (more network cards), an interface may get an address of improper interface in the data package, so its response may be sent on improper route and it will not reach the client (SmartServer).

In the second case (transfer through router), a local address may be stored to the data package in target network (where KNX interface has no sense, or is duplicated one, respectively). In such case, the interface either is not able to send the response at all, or will send it to another equipment.
If the above-mentioned troubles occur, it is recommended to use tunnelling-NAT or routing kind of communication.

text.p: If the connection is configured and despite of it, the server cannot be connected, the simplest way is to use the diagnostic listings (see chapter ). Debugging listings will provide information, based on which it is possible to determine the reason of troubles easier.

Listings connected with KNX interface originate from KNX/EibNet.Connection source and they cover establishing and disconnection of connection, data transfer (in all modes) and control information. Listings with word CONNECT and LISTENING relate to establishing of connection, listings with word DISCONNECT relate to disconnection of the connection. Data transferred by tunnel connection contain words SEND or RECEIVE, data transferred with help of routing contain words ROUTED IN or ROUTED OUT.

During its duration, each connection with KNX interface is designated by number. An interface assigns the number of connection, usually each new connection gets the number higher by one. The number is important for diagnostics of communication with KNX, because it must stay unchanged during one connection. If the number of connection is changed in debugging listings, then something is probably wrong in the communication. Following example shows listings of connection (only some lines are selected from the record) with number 99:
text.p.type: [3.450] t KNX/EibNet.Connection: CONNECTed in TUNNELING mode: 99 10.0.0.6:3671 [3.700] t KNX/EibNet.Connection: RECEIVE 99 group: 2/1/30 [3.970] t KNX/EibNet.Connection: SEND 99 group: 2/1/30 true [4.241] t KNX/EibNet.Connection: DISCONNECT request: 99 10.0.0.6:3671 [4.251] t KNX/EibNet.Connection: DISCONNECTed: 99 10.0.0.6:3671
text.p: The example contains a successfully established connection. A connection, which cannot be established, is shown in following record (two examples are shown):
text.p.type: [0.644] t KNX/EibNet.Connection: CONNECT request: 10.0.0.16:3671 [0.661] t KNX/EibNet.Connection: CONNECT timeout ... [9.130] t KNX/EibNet.Connection: CONNECT request: 10.0.0.6:3671 [9.140] t KNX/EibNet.Connection: CONNECT failure: 36 10.0.0.6:3671 [9.140] t KNX/EibNet.Connection: DISCONNECTed: 0 10.0.0.6:3671
text.p: In the first case, the server was not connected with KNX interface, because no response came in the frame of determined time (timeout). The most frequent reasons of this behaviour are: IP address or port addresses of the interface wrongly introduced, interface disconnected from network and network unavailability of interface (e.g. if the interface is behind NAT interface, etc.).

dl.caption: In the second unsuccessful case the server interface found the connection, but the interface refused the connection with error 36. Error codes are the part of KNX standard (KNX Std 3.8.1), which currently defines following errors:

dd.p: Interface does not support requested kind of connection. E.g., the server requests the tunnel connection, but the interface does not know it.
Interface does not support requested setting of connection. Presently not used.
Interface does not allow the connection, because its maximum number of connections is already exhausted.

This error is the most frequent one, because current KNX interface allows only one tunnel connection. If something else (other server, ETS) is connected to the interface, then connection of the server is not successful. The error may be caused also by outages of power-supply or network: if the server will not terminate the connection (e.g. at forced switch-off of the computer), then the interface waits for two minutes, before it allow to establish a new connection.

dl.caption: A simple procedure for finding out of problems with connection may be, e.g., as follows:
dl.dt: Attempt for connection finishes with error timeout

dd.p: Check the network cable (ping on interface address must be successful), check if the interface is powered on.

Verify, if interface is running (if it is supplied, etc.). Make sure that you use the proper address and the interface port. If the interface is in local network, then with help of discover tool (part of server installation) find out addresses and ports of available interfaces.

If the interface is in a foreign network (if you are connected through Internet), then verify, if the UDP transfer in both directions (outside and inside) of selected port is allowed on routers between the server and the interface. Verify, if you are using the tunnelling-ACK kind of connection in such case.
If you are using the routing kind of connection, then verify, if routers and switches between the server and the interface support and properly work with IP multicast packets.

dl.dt: Attempt for connection finishes with error failure: XX

dd.p: If you are using the tunnelling or tunnelling-ACK kinds of connection, then verify, if another server, ETS, or some other program is not connected to the interface. In an affirmative case, disconnect it.

Make sure that during last two minutes an outage of server did not occur (forced switching-off of the computer, forced stopping of the server process). In affirmative case, wait two minutes or switch off and switch on the interface power supply.

text.p: All examples contain real data, including time stamps. The length of operations or waiting is thus easily readable.
T_CON = KNX interface acknowledge, R_CON = target KNX device acknowledge, seq = sequence number of sent or received packets.

section.title: Location of source data and access

text.p: For administration and for user’s web pages connected with data from KNX, the SmartServer provides an embedded web server. Administrative part is protected by name and password, user’s web pages are free available. The server runs on IP port 6005.

Administrative part of the server is available on the address http://[server]:6005/SmartServer, user’s part of the server is available on the address http://[server]:6005/SmartServer/User ([server] must be replaced with the name or address of the computer, for a local computer there will be valid, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:6005/SmartServer). All files, which should be available with help of server, must be stored in User folder (and in subfolders, for details, see ).

Administrative interface is distributed to several pages protected by name and password. After insertion URL http://[server]:6005/SmartServer to the address line of Internet browser and clicking on Private pages link the SmartServer enters to the administrative interface. Following page Login requires input of login data. After the SmartServer installation, the name admin and the password admin is the valid couple.
The login to the administrative interface is timely limited and expires after 30 minutes of inactivity.

dl.caption: The administrative interface consists from following pages:

dd.p: Introductory page with quick survey of status of server and its licence.

The possibility of connection and disconnection of the SmartServer with/from KNX interface is important. E.g., if KNX interface is shared and used currently as for configuration, as for programming of the equipment in KNX, then the SmartServer must be disconnected before ETS connection and connected again after completion of programming (otherwise the SmartServer will not provide valid data to clients).

dl.dd:
Page for setting of the server configuration. It is possible to switch on and to switch off both client interface (SDAP client, XMLSocket client) and it is possible to change the server configuration.
The interface does not allow to load the configuration with help of browser or file and the configuration must enter to computer with the SmartServer by another way (with help of RDP, etc.). The configuration is changed after specification of the route to the configuration file (actual configuration file is filled in advance) and press of Apply push-button. E.g., at modification of setting of connection or at addition of new data objects, the configuration file is modified first (the new one is prepared) and is consequently applied by press of Apply push-button, without necessity to restart the SmartServer service.
With help of Save... linkthe actual configuration file can be loaded and stored in local computer.
Under the line with configuration and push-buttons, there is an area with listing of errors found out at loading of the configuration. If the configuration is OK (e.g. if it was checked in advance with help of checkcfg installed tool), always one line will be added about successful loading of the configuration. Loading of configuration with help of Use push-button replaces only the configuration related to data objects of the server and to communication with KNX. The server accepts the system configuration, i.e. the configuration file section ([log], [datalog] (), [web] () and [users] ()), at its start only.

dd.p: The page displays the history of data operation of the server. In the list arranged from the newest events to the oldest ones there occurs following eventsUPDATE (receipt of data from data bus), SET OK (successful record), SET FAILED (starting of the record failed, e.g., if the SmartServer is not just connected to the data bus) and SET ERROR (the record was started, but finished with error).

Only such data objects occurs in the history, which was created in the configuration with help of logged_objects, logged_objects_on_change, logged_object and logged_object_on_change parameters (see chapter ).

The page with system records will be mostly empty. Especially debugging and diagnostic listings are included among records, which are not listed, if they are not switched on. If the listings are switched on in [log] section, (see ), they will appear just here.
Simple page allowing directly record and load the server data objects.

Read value from EIB requires insertion of the group address (e.g. 3/2/3) to the field on the left from Load push-button and its press. The SmartServer will write the value or information about loading error.

Write value to EIB works analogously, nevertheless, there is further requested an insertion of recorded value in the second field. E.g., if logic one should be recorded to the bit address 3/1/1, it is set to the field with value true. After press of Write push-button, the SmartServer will announce the result of the record (and on Data history page one can check the feature of the writing).

text.p: All files in Web/User folder of the installation folder may be displayed without a login. E.g., index.html example file (part of the server installation), present in this folder, will be available in local computer as http://127.0.0.1:6005/SmartServer/User/index.html.

Among files (current static HTML, figures, styles), there may be located files with pt.xml extension (e.g. example.pt.xml, which is a part of installation), which the SmartServer processes dynamically and thus allows to input live data of data objects from EIB inside their contents. pt.xml files are XML, therefore they must be well formed and for use in the SmartServer they must have defined XML namespace http://www.smartcontrol.cz/2008/XML/Web/PageTemplate. If it will have proper suffix and wrong namespace, the Smart-Server will not process it as dynamical one and will not input live data to it.
For creation of own user’s pages with live data there is recommended for all cases to create a copy of the example file and modify this copy.

Live data get to the page with help of get function closed to signs ${ a }. The SmartServer searches these signs and replaces them with actual value. Similarly it is possible to record a value to EIB using set function. The record of value requires the user’s activity (press of push-button, reference), therefore the SmartServer in user’s dynamic (pt.xml) pages accepts set function as parameter of reference on page (on another one or on itself). It is also possible to use a selection command (pt :choose) inside dynamic pages, which allows to create the different contents of the page according to different values of logic data objects.

text.p: From examples it is obvious that signs specific for the SmartServer are clearly separated (pt:...) and that the rest of the text is a current, not limited HTML. This is also the reason, why to use in pt.xml files all HTML structures including styles, scripts, etc.

Browsing of web pages is oriented to users. A user will select an address, a reference, to which he/she wants to move, and the browser will ask the server for data and the server will return them to the browser. Between requirements the browser and the web server do not keep any connection and they do not know about each other.

For display of data from the SmartServer it may be useful, if, from time to time, the browser itself will ask the web server for new data. HTTP/HTML technology has no standard for this case, nevertheless, the most of current browsers respects meta refresh tag for this purpose (without regard to the fact that meta refresh is not recommended by W3C).
Use of meta refresh sign is best illustrated on example (the source file, 05 get refresh.pt.xml and the result sent to the browser are ranked one behind each other):

text.p: Addition of <meta refresh.../> tag will cause that the browser will ask the web server for new data each five seconds.

SDAP (Simple Data Access Protocol) allows a remote access to the server data items and concurrently also allows to perform some administrative tasks. SDAP is a text line protocol transferred with help of TCP from the SmartServer on port 6007. After connection to the server, no control data are transferred by the protocol. After its establishing, the connection is permanent till its termination by the client. In case of unrecognised outage of the network, the server will complete the connection to 2 minutes, approximately.

SDAP confirms (response) all orders/requirements for server (request). If the confirmation will not come after sending of the command, the command was neither accepted, nor elaborated. All commands and responses are completed with signs CR and LF.
SDAP response to requirements by the line with status code, behind which, in some responses, there may follow more next lines with information. The format of the status code is:
text.p.type: XXX.Y
text.p: or
text.p.type: XXX.Y N
text.p: where XXX.Y is the status code itself, N is the number of following lines with next information and Y is an optional part further specifying the place of error (e.g. number of parameter, which was erroneous).

dl.caption: Meaning of single status codes is as follows (2XX are affirmative responses, 3XX are temporary statuses, 4XX are errors on client’s side and 5XX are errors on server’s side):

dd.p: The request was completely processed.
The request was processed, nevertheless, the server has no connection with EIB and data were only stored in the cache server.
Data advised by the server.
Operation is running.
Missing command in the request.
The request contains an unknown command.
The command is known, but its subcommand is not known.
Wrong number of parameters.
Wrong value of the parameter.
Unknown, non-existing source (e.g. non-existing data item).
Internal non-distinguished server error.
The service is not available (e.g. server is not running, etc.).
Non-supported requirement or command. The command is allowed in SDAP, but the server does not support it.
The server terminates the connection with the client (but continues in activity). No return code.

Data are recorded to the server. The command format is set group value, where the group is the data item of the server (some group address) and the value is the value corresponding to the data type of the item. Example: set 3/1/0 true.
Possible return codes are: 200, 201, 405 a 5XX.
Example of communication to server:
Loads data from the server. The command format is get group, where the group is the server data item (some group address). Example: get 3/1/1.

The server responds with return code 200 N, 201 N, 405 and 5XX, whereas N designates the number of following lines with values of data items in the form of the group value. The value is the value loaded from the server data item.
Example of communication to server:
The server starts, possible return codes are 200, 300 and 5XX.
The server stops (is disconnected from EIB), possible return codes are 200 and 5XX.

It subscribes the data object for advising, the server announces itself to the client the changes in object data. The command format is advise group, where group is the server data object (some group address) or advise all. advise all subscribes all server data objects for taking. Example: advise 3/1/1 or advise all.
The server responds with return code 200, 405 and 5XX.
Example of communication with the server:

After subscribing of advising of values, the server monitors changes in taken data objects and in case of change it sends a message to the client with return code 202 N, where N designates the number of following lines with values of data objects in the form of group value. The value is the new value of the server data object.
Example of delivery of advised data:
Cancels advising of the data object. The command format is unadvise group, where group is the server data object (group address), or unadvise all (if advising of all data items is cancelled).
The server responds with return code 200, 405 and 5XX.
Example of communication with the server:

text.p: XMLSocket interface allows the data exchange with the server. XMLSocket is a line text protocol, which is transferred TCP from the server on port 6006 with help of TCP. Each line of the protocol contains well formed XML with data details. After its establishing, the connection is permanent till its termination by the client. In case of unrecognised outage of the network, the server will complete the connection to 2 minutes, approximately.
XML in the protocol has following format (example of real XML):
text.p.type: <xmlsocket> <notify> <name>3/1/0</name> <value>true</value> </notify> </xmlsocket>
text.p: The group address in the name tag need not be known to the server, in such case the server ignores the requirement. Inside one xmlsocket tag, there may be more notify tags, which allows to transfer more values by one communication.

XMLSocket protocol is especially the event one, the server sends to the client the data at their change. Nevertheless, the client has also the possibility to ask the server for data, e.g. when the animation in Flash starts. The format of requesting of data and value from the server is (example of real XML):
text.p.type: <xmlsocket> <ask> <name>2/0/0</name> </ask> </xmlsocket>
text.p: There may be also more ask tags inside the xmlsocket one, so the client may ask for more data together by one communication.

The last option of XMLSocket interface is driving of EIB/KNX connection. There are tags <connect/> and <disconnect/> which connect or disconnect the server and the EIB/KNX interface. Examples of connect and disconnect request are:
text.p.type: <xmlsocket> <connect/> </xmlsocket>
<xmlsocket> <disconnect/> </xmlsocket>

text.p: In the SmartServer installation there are included two examples of clients. The first client (Examples\Philips Pronto) uses SDAP for communication, the second client (Examples\Adobe Flash) uses XMLSocket for communication.

Philips Pronto is an universal remote controller with support of graphics, touch display, WiFi communication and full support of programming. The support for general programs allows to create in Pronto the communication interface for SDAP, with which information from EIB will get inside the Pronto application and vice versa, and with help of which the program (user) may remotely control EIB.

JavaScript is the programming language of Pronto (the same language is used for client programming in Internet pages), ProntoEdit Professional serves for programming of Pronto, the program is free available for loading on pages http://www.pronto.philips.com (where, of course, a lot of information about Pronto and its use can be found).

dl.caption: Following files are in the example:

dd.p: A file with frame of application for Pronto. The application can be directly loaded to ProntoEdit and further modified. The application contains several displays for the A/V control and two displays (inside EIB equipment), which allow to control lights and blinds.

In the example, there is immediately obvious the kind of communication with EIB: The main JavaScript connected with the EIB equipment assures the communication with help of SDAP; what and how should be communicatedthis complies each of both immersed screens at its display to the main JavaScript and it itself then reach on incoming values.
The main communication script is stored in EIB/EIB Properties branch in Advanced tab.

The main JavaScript are independently separated from previous file for simpler view. IP_ADDRESS variable is defined in introduction of the script; at the use it must be set to proper address of the SmartServer.

System.SetReadObjects, System.PageUpdate and System.ConnectionCheck are the part of script of this method. These methods use scripts of pages for setting of communication of requested data items, reaction to their value and the new value and reaction to actual status of the communication.
Connection with the server is repeatedly established and terminated, because Pronto Script at transfer to StandBy mode incorrectly closes the TCP connection.
JavaScript from the page for control of lights. In Template.xcf, the script is recorded in EIB/Lights branch in Advanced tab.
The above-mentioned methods from Main.js script are clearly used in the script.
JavaScript from the push-button for switching-on and switching-off of the light. In Template.xcf, the script is recorded in Templates/Lights branch, in Light push-button, in Actions tab.
The script for the change of status of the server data object refers to variables defined in Page.js script.
JavaScript from the push-button for dimming (reduction of brightness). In Template.xcf, the script is recorded in Templates/Lights branch, in Dimming push-button, in Actions tab.
The script for dimming (at holding of the push-button the brightness is continuously reduced), the script refers to variables defined in Page.js script.
JavaScript from the push-button for blind close. In Template.xcf, the script is recorded in Templates/Blinds branch, in BlindsDown push-button, in Actions tab.
The script starts long movement (CentralLong) and counts time of button pressing. If the button is released in two seconds, the script stops the movement by writing a value to CentralStep object.

text.p: Adobe Flash is, similarly as Pronto, fully programmable. By coincidence of accidents, Macromedia for Flash also used the JavaScript program language, even when it was commercially named as ActionScript. ActionScript directly supports XMLSocket interface, so the data exchange with the SmartServer is easy (it lies in break and assembling of XML).

dl.caption: Following files are in the example for Adobe Flash:

dd.p: File with example of the main communication script, which as analyses XML, as calls animation procedures for needed elements announcing changes of the value (to elements, which are registered).

Implementation of communication is encased to SmartServerConnector class, the class of program in Flash offers Connect, Close, AskValue and Send methods and onConnect, onClose and onReceive events (which may be followed by the program).
File with example of assembling and sending of data from Flash to the SmartServer.

The script, for example, defines Connection variable, which is the communication class from SmartServerConnector.as class, and calls its Connect method. In real application, this code will be probably located in another place, then in servicing of user’s event of the push-button.

A source file of very simple animation with two push-buttons (one for loading of the value, the second one for the record). The file contains reference to above mentioned SmartServerConnector.as main script and uses them.

text.p: Example scripts can be inserted to application for Adobe Flash, e.g. using clipboard.

dl.caption: Except of examples, the main program and files of the SmartServer web interface contain several tools, which may help at setting and diagnostics. All are installed as the part of the SmartServer and are located in its installation directory. They are:

dd.p: Program for activation of licences. Its usage is described in chapter .
A tool for browsing of local network, the result of work is the list of found Eib-Net/IP devices. The program will find interfaces and routers. Example of the program output:
